summary: Checked the reported Pacific and Atlantic schemes against their laws. The Marshall Islands really did sell passports under its Citizenship Act (1989 amendment, fee $200,000 cut to $100,000, suspended 1996, repealed 2001); Samoa has a real but little-used investor route (WST 4m investment, 3 years' residence, since 2017); Papua New Guinea (2016) and Cape Verde (since 1992, reworded 2023) have only discretionary investor naturalisation with no price set, and Cape Verde also has a 2018 Green Card residence for property buyers (EUR 80,000/120,000). For Nauru the two amending Acts (2025, 2026) were found, and the budget papers give the first official figures: AU$0.24m revenue in FY2024/25 and about AU$3.4-3.7m in FY2025/26 against AU$9m budgets, with 103 applications, 52 approvals and 9 rejections (budget speech). Botswana's investor citizenship bill passed Parliament in Dec 2025 and Ghana's 2026 investment bill orders a CBI law, but neither has an operating programme or official price.

programs.name: Marshall Islands sale of passports and citizenship (Citizenship Act 1984 s. 404(4), 'passport investment and sales program')
programs.notes: Real and legal: s. 404 of the Citizenship Act 1984 let Cabinet naturalise people for distinguished service or 'in the public interest', and a subsection (4) on the sale of passports was added by P.L. 1989-37; P.L. 1989-68 lowered the fee for a passport from $200,000 to $100,000 (currency not named). Cabinet suspended the programme on 20 June 1996 (reported), citing misleading advertising in Hong Kong, Taiwan and China and US concerns; the subsection was repealed on 18 Oct 2001. An academic report dates sales to 1987-1996 and estimates about 2,000 citizenships sold, mainly to Chinese buyers. Unofficial agents sold passports for $30,000 with false promises of US entry. Today s. 404 allows at most five discretionary naturalisations a year. 'launched' is the year of the enabling amendment; the amending acts and any official count were not found.

programs.name: Samoa citizenship by investment (Citizenship Investment Act 2015)
programs.notes: Not an instant passport: investors worth at least WST 2.5 million who commit to invest WST 4 million in listed sectors within 3 years (70% first held in a Samoan fixed deposit) get a 3-year permanent residence permit, then may apply for citizenship if they spent 15 days a year in Samoa and kept to the investment plan. Run by a Citizenship Investment Committee chaired by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour. Fees: WST 120,000 application and WST 20,000 due diligence for the principal applicant. The Committee must report yearly to Parliament (s. 22), but no report or official count was found (a press report that the scheme drew almost no interest could not be read). In Oct 2025 applicants tied to foreign governments were barred (reported). Separately, Samoan passports (not citizenship) were sold illegally in Hong Kong and China in the 1990s (academic report).

programs.name: Papua New Guinea naturalisation of investors (Constitution s. 67(4)(b); Citizenship Act s. 6B)
programs.notes: Not a priced citizenship-by-investment programme: since 2016 the minister may, at discretion and subject to the Citizenship Advisory Committee, naturalise a person with the capital and commitment to invest, create jobs and transfer skills, waiving one of the ordinary naturalisation requirements (s. 67(5), which keeps the others). No investment amount is set in law; the fee is to be set by instrument (not found). No figures on investors naturalised were found. 'launched' is the certification date of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act; the constitutional amendment was certified on 29 Aug 2016.

programs.name: Cabo Verde nationality by investment (Lei 33/X/2023 art. 14; formerly 'economic nationality', Lei 80/III/90 art. 12(3)-(4) as amended in 1992)
programs.notes: A legal route, not an operating programme with a price. From 1992 investors creating jobs could get the rights of citizens without political rights (Law 41/IV/92), later reworded as citizenship (Law 64/IV/92). The 2023 Nationality Act (art. 14) replaced this with nationality for 'relevant' investments (job-creating projects, tourism property, regional development companies, capital in investment funds, etc.) plus effective ties (language or regular stays); minimum amounts are left to a future law. An academic report (Jan 2026) says the special regulation is still pending. Industry claims of USD 80,000 or 200,000 routes have no legal basis found. No statistics.

programs.name: Cabo Verde Green Card - permanent residence for property buyers (Lei 30/IX/2018)
programs.notes: Permanent residence for foreigners (with spouse and dependants) who buy built or under-construction residential property of at least EUR 80,000 in a municipality with below-average GDP per capita, or EUR 120,000 elsewhere, paid with money transferred from abroad. The card is renewed every 5 years, then every 10 after the second renewal, as long as the property is kept; property-tax and pension-income exemptions. Issued by the Direction of Foreigners and Borders (DEF). 'launched' is the publication date; the law entered into force 30 days later. The implementing regulation and any count of cards issued were not found, so the current status is not confirmed.

Set up by the Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Act 2024 (No. 15 of 2024, certified 20 Aug 2024); prices in Regulations SL 28 of 2024 (gazetted 30 Oct 2024). Unveiled at COP29 on 13 Nov 2024 and launched by the President in Singapore on 28 Nov 2024; the IMF gives 2025 as inception year. One route: a non-refundable contribution to the Treasury Fund, applications only through licensed agents, run by a Program Office; the budget papers say it was designed and is run with Henley & Partners. Amended by Act No. 50 of 2025 (Cabinet sets contributions and may grant temporary 'Special Project' discounts) and Act No. 13 of 2026 (the Minister may refuse applications directly). Prices were restructured on 29 Jan 2026 (USD 115,000 single applicant) and a temporary USD 90,000 discount applies to 31 Dec 2026. No programme statistics are published, but the 2026-27 budget speech reported 103 applications, 52 approvals and 9 rejections in FY2025-26. Revenue: AU$0.24 million in FY2024/25 and about AU$3.4-3.7 million in FY2025/26, against AU$9 million budgeted each year.
